1.2 Output: Script that verifies the election artifacts generated in Output 1.1 using one of the verifier reference implementations.
Acceptance criteria: Script runs in a Nix environment, reads a set of election artifacts, and either returns 0 (yes, the entire election is valid) or throws an error message saying which section/property failed to verify. Known good artifacts from the ElectionGuard project should verify. The artifacts generated by the script in Output 1.1 should verify. Good artifacts broken manually (for example by changing or removing a vote, or changing one of the final tallies) should fail to verify.
Note: after digging into it more I realized the “known good” official artifacts don’t come in any one format. They’ve been evolving each time there’s an agreement to test ElectionGuard on a new election. They also include a bunch of probably-not-relevant-to-Cardano things like definitions of boundaries of congressional districts, political parties, and so on. So I haven’t tried to write code to verify them. Would it be possible to remove that requirement?
The other minor thing that doesn’t technically meet the requirement is the verifier script logs errors to a file + a JSON summary rather than throwing an exception and printing them. I think it’s more useful this way but could change it fairly easily if you want.

ms.report:
A. Output: 2.1: Documentation of the design: smart contracts, on-chain data, off-chain data.
Acceptance criteria: One or more markdown docs (with figures where helpful), and one whiteboard-style video. The video should include enough detail that people already familiar with Cardano and EUTXO will feel they generally understand the design without reading the docs, but shouldn't go over ~10 minutes. The docs should be detailed enough that a programmer would be able to say what each file and smart contract operation does, but not be an exhaustive reference with all function parameters, schemas etc.
Evidence:
https://github.com/jefdaj/electionguard-cardano/tree/trunk/milestone2/design
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zWpfJSx9b1I
I think this is the only part of the requirements I didn't quite meet: the "short" video is 15min. I tried to make it short but couldn't think what more to cut and still have it make sense. Can always cut some more if needed though! My current feeling is that a separate series of very short shorts explaining one little aspect of the system at a time published after the M3 demo will be more effective at getting non-developers interested, and anyone actually writing Aiken code probably wants detailed examples.
Edit: Dev Update #6 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qe0vyI1Zazo) also partially addresses the design. It shows how the offchain code depends on the onchain code.
B. Output: 2.2: Script that build and uploads the on-chain + off-chain data for a single election.
Acceptance criteria:
 * Runs in a Nix environment
 * Deploys an election contract to one of the public testnets
 * Submits transactions updating the contract for each step in the election
 * Uploads matching file(s) to IPFS at each step
 * Does not need to be hooked up to electionguard yet; static files from a previous run are OK
